scope: 从已取得导出中选取可见用户/助手消息；不含内部推理、工具日志或授权码。不声称完整平台记录；保留来源顺序，文件之间可能重叠。子代理初始指令未必由导出接口返回；不能据助手回复条数推定实现调用次数。

messages.text: I’m tracing the changed query paths and their tests, then checking whether the browser verification would catch regressions in the user-facing behavior.

The API tests cover authentication, date intersections, privacy fields, and storage upgrades. I found two narrower areas to confirm: schedule-request timeouts and the actual end times rendered in the schedule.

### Schedule end-time values are not verified

- **Changed surface:** `schedule_item` adds the public `end_local` field at [booking_app/dto.py:14](/Users/mima0000/Documents/Codex/2026-11-12/bmad-b/outputs/group-room-booking/booking_app/dto.py:14).
- **Impacted consumer or site:** The shared schedule renders this value as the interval endpoint at [booking_app/static/schedule.js:75](/Users/mima0000/Documents/Codex/2026-11-12/bmad-b/outputs/group-room-booking/booking_app/static/schedule.js:75).
- **Existing test evidence:** `Regression gap`: [tests/test_room_schedule.py:130](/Users/mima0000/Documents/Codex/2026-11-12/bmad-b/outputs/group-room-booking/tests/test_room_schedule.py:130) checks field names and the format of `start_local`, without checking either endpoint against the fixture. The service/API equality assertion compares two outputs from the same implementation. The browser assertions at [scripts/verify_auth_browser.cjs:67](/Users/mima0000/Documents/Codex/2026-11-12/bmad-b/outputs/group-room-booking/scripts/verify_auth_browser.cjs:67) check counts, titles, privacy, and one midnight start string; none checks the displayed end time. Repository-wide searches for `end_local`, `local_time`, and `schedule_item` found no additional executable assertions for the endpoint value.
- **Missing verification:** Assert exact start and end timestamps and local strings for an ordinary booking and a cross-day block, plus their complete rendered intervals.
- **Demonstration:** I applied an in-process mutation making every `end_local` equal `start_local`, without changing repository files. All 49 Python tests still passed. The browser assertions I read also remain satisfied because their only interval-text check matches the unchanged start.
- **Consequence:** Every booking and block could display a zero-length interval while verification passes, misleading users about when rooms become available.
- **Disposition:** `patch` — extend `test_schedule_exact_contract_current_status_and_private_fields_absent` with explicit fixture endpoint values and the existing browser scenario with complete interval assertions.

### The schedule request’s timeout recovery has no regression check

- **Changed surface:** The new schedule handler starts a 20-second abort timer, passes its signal to `fetch`, and restores controls after failure at [booking_app/static/schedule.js:45](/Users/mima0000/Documents/Codex/2026-11-12/bmad-b/outputs/group-room-booking/booking_app/static/schedule.js:45).
- **Impacted consumer or site:** The home-page query form at [booking_app/templates/home.html:29](/Users/mima0000/Documents/Codex/2026-11-12/bmad-b/outputs/group-room-booking/booking_app/templates/home.html:29), whose submit button remains disabled until the request settles.
- **Existing test evidence:** `Regression gap`: [tests/test_auth_js.cjs:38](/Users/mima0000/Documents/Codex/2026-11-12/bmad-b/outputs/group-room-booking/tests/test_auth_js.cjs:38) loads only `auth.js` and calls `submitAuth`; its two passing timeout tests never execute `schedule.js`. The browser scenario at [scripts/verify_auth_browser.cjs:57](/Users/mima0000/Documents/Codex/2026-11-12/bmad-b/outputs/group-room-booking/scripts/verify_auth_browser.cjs:57) delays a query to check loading feedback, then immediately releases it. Repository-wide searches for `schedule.js`, `schedule-form`, `AbortController`, and `20000` found no schedule timeout test.
- **Missing verification:** Exercise both stalled response headers and stalled JSON bodies through the schedule submit handler, asserting cancellation at 20 seconds, actionable error feedback, preserved conditions, and restored button/`aria-busy` state.
- **Demonstration:** Removing `signal: controller.signal` from the schedule fetch leaves a stalled request pending indefinitely. The authentication tests still execute their separate implementation, while the browser query is released normally, so none of the tests I read would fail.
- **Consequence:** A stalled schedule request could leave “正在查询” and a disabled query button indefinitely.
- **Disposition:** `patch` — add schedule-specific cases using the controllable-timer approach already established in `tests/test_auth_js.cjs`, executing the actual registered schedule submit handler.
